clue.text: You may get the point of this today

definitions.text: You may get the point of this today

parts.words: You may get the point of this today
parts.note: on Valentine's Day the winged love god's dart is what strikes a smitten person, so its point is something you might literally feel

explanation.surface: A remark about being on the receiving end of something sharp on a particular day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like getting the meaning of something, but it is the sharp tip of the love god's dart; 'today' places the clue on 14 February.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the dart that makes its target fall in love, felt on Valentine's Day.

clue.text: Hundred and fifty select few endlessly bathed in a warm glow

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the word for the select few is cut off

parts.note: the elite are a select few

explanation.surface: A description of a privileged group lounging in comfortable warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' removes the last E of ELITE, leaving ELIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A room lit by candles is softly illuminated by flickering warm flames.

clue.text: Exercise right before panel to give false evidence

indicators.note: before places the first pieces ahead of the panel word in the answer

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a jury is a panel of citizens judging a case

explanation.surface: A courtroom scene in which someone works out before facing the jurors and then lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give' is a link here, joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying under oath in court is the legal offence of giving false testimony.

clue.text: What are the odds of dryish fizzy drink leading to a tummy ache?

indicators.note: the odds of takes the first, third and fifth letters of the following word

parts.note: Pepsi is a brand of fizzy cola drink

explanation.surface: A question about the chances that a dry sparkling drink will upset the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What are the odds' sounds like a bet, but 'odds' picks the odd letters of dryish, giving DYS. 'leading to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion, a medical term for an upset stomach, is commonly felt as a tummy ache.

clue.text: Start off voting dole out

indicators.note: Start off says the first letter of the voting word is removed

parts.note: a ballot is a vote or the process of voting

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin by voting on how benefits should be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the B from BALLOT leaves the answer. 'dole' looks like unemployment benefit, but 'dole out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion or distribute shares is to hand them out, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Following run on icy surface winter sports enthusiast is more reckless

indicators.note: Following says the skiing enthusiast comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the surface of a word is its top or first letter, here of icy

parts.note: a skier enjoys winter sports on snow

explanation.surface: A skier on an icy slope is being more daring than is wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surface' gives the first letter of icy, I; 'is' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking more chances or being more hazardous is the comparative of a word meaning dangerous.

clue.text: Wind you and I have commonly

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: commonly signals a casual or dialect pronunciation in which the opening H is dropped

explanation.surface: A colloquial remark that you and I have something in common.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the H of have gives 'AVE, as in casual speech. 'Wind' looks like a breeze, but it is the verb meaning to twist in and out.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind a path through obstacles is to thread or zigzag through them.

clue.text: Some gigolo! Nerdy one with no friends

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a nerdy kept man who has no companions.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person who keeps to themselves and has no companions.

clue.text: Nothing's on screen that Shakespeare wrote

parts.note: love is nothing in tennis scoring, and the 's stands for is
a blind is a screen over a window

explanation.surface: A comment that nothing being shown on screen was written by Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. 'Nothing's' must be read as nothing is, giving two words. The phrase appears in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase about lovers failing to see faults is a line from The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Tricky task: sell a pitch

indicators.note: tricky suggests something intricate, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Selling is a difficult job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' rearranges the letters of TASK SELL A.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales pitch is persuasive patter a salesperson uses to win a customer.

clue.text: Recipe for disaster in affectionate gesture by horseman?

parts.note: a kiss is an affectionate gesture
by as in a work by an author, meaning belonging to or of
Death is one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse

explanation.surface: A loving gesture made by a rider leads to catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseman' is not any rider but one of the biblical Four Horsemen.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an action certain to bring about ruin or failure.

clue.text: Head of the Arts replaced by very predatory creature

indicators.note: Head of points to the first letter of the arts word as the one to change
replaced by says that letter is swapped for the very abbreviation

parts.note: the arts collectively are culture

explanation.surface: The head of an arts body is replaced by a ruthless predator.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the C of CULTURE for V.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey that feeds on carrion; also used of predatory people.

clue.text: Minute outwardly powerless muscles

parts.note: a trice is a moment, as in 'in a trice'

indicators.note: outwardly takes just the outside letters of powerless

explanation.surface: A tiny, weak person has muscles only on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like tiny, but it is the noun meaning a moment. 'outwardly' gives PS, the outer letters of powerless.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-headed muscles at the back of the upper arm are plural in form.

clue.text: Popular place for mosaic perhaps

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to lay is to place or put down

explanation.surface: A popular spot to find a mosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to put down.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is an example of decoration set into a surface, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Dodgy poseur embracing her is fantasy figure

indicators.note: embracing says the rearranged letters wrap around her
dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady poser with his arm around a woman is a figure of fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges POSEUR into SUPERO, which then holds HER: SUPER-HER-O.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic-book hero with special powers is a fictional figure from fantasy.

clue.text: Bonfire temperature's hot beside unusual chrysanth

parts.note: a pyre is a bonfire, especially for burning a body
T is the abbreviation for temperature
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
rum means odd or unusual in British slang

explanation.surface: A gardener notes the bonfire's heat next to an exotic chrysanthemum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside' is a link. 'rum' is old British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like flower of the chrysanthemum family, source of a natural insecticide.

clue.text: Count out and pay with small change and no tip

indicators.note: small change suggests a slight rearrangement of the remaining letters
no tip says the first letter of the pay word is removed

parts.note: to remunerate is to pay

explanation.surface: Counting out payment in coins without leaving a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R gives EMUNERATE; 'small change' swaps its M and N. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To list items one by one or number them is to count them out.

clue.text: City and church make public transport available for invalids

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
to air an opinion is to make it public

explanation.surface: A city and church provide public transport for the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public transport' seems a unit, but 'make public' gives AIR and the definition is the rest. BATH is a spa city in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded wheeled chair once used to push invalids about, named after the spa city.

clue.text: Talk English at the French country house in the Dordogne?

parts.note: to chat is to talk
au is French for 'at the' (masculine)

explanation.surface: A conversation in English at a French country home.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the Dordogne is just one example of a French setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a castle or a grand country house.

clue.text: Drinks and sandwiches

definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for everyone in a group
a sandwich made from two slices of bread counts as one unit of this

explanation.definitionFit: A pub round is drinks for all; a round of sandwiches is a unit made from two slices.

clue.text: Give up burden

definitions.meaning: to abstain from or stop doing something
the burden of a song is its chorus repeated after each verse

explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to give something up; a song's burden is its repeated chorus.

clue.text: I'm left in show which is endless graft

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: in puts the left letter inside the shortened show
endless says the final letter of the show word is cut off

parts.note: a panto is a pantomime, a British Christmas stage show

explanation.surface: Someone left in a show complains it never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts PANTO to PANT, which holds L: P-L-ANT. A panto is a British Christmas family show. 'which is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A graft is tissue or an organ surgically inserted into the body.

clue.text: Claim some characters in Donizetti's opera are contrary

indicators.note: are contrary says that run is read the wrong way round
some characters in says the answer is a run of letters inside the following words

explanation.surface: A suggestion that some singers in a Donizetti opera are being awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: The run TISOP sits across the words, and 'are contrary' turns it round. 'characters' looks like roles in an opera, but it means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit something is to put it forward as a claim or assumption.

clue.text: Underground root's original potato maybe

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground railway

indicators.note: original takes the first letter of the word root

explanation.surface: An underground root's ancestor might be the potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' looks like soil, but it is the London Underground, known as the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is an example of a swollen underground stem used for storage.

clue.text: Stuff with taleggio — originally a fine cheese

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the word taleggio

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: Filling something with taleggio, which began life as a fine cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a verb meaning to fill, but it is the noun meaning fabric. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp silk fabric; stuff is an old word for woven material.

clue.text: Break up most of dismal coal while it glows

indicators.note: most of says the word dismal loses its last letters

parts.note: an ember is a glowing piece of coal

explanation.surface: Breaking up dreary coal while it is still glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of DISMAL is DISM.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to cut or tear apart, breaking something up into pieces.

clue.text: Crush in a party

parts.note: a bash is a lively party

explanation.surface: Being caught in a crowd at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' looks like a dense crowd, but it is the verb meaning to humiliate. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to embarrass or humble them, to crush their confidence.

clue.text: Unlikely mature crone will provide you with ideal relationship

indicators.note: unlikely suggests something improbable, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An improbable older woman offers you the perfect partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlikely' rearranges MATURE CRONE. 'will provide you with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine love between partners, the idealised kind found in romantic fiction.
